title: Surveying and Benchmarking Foundation Models for Time Series Classification
content: Foundation models enable the reuse of pretrained knowledge across time series classification (TSC) tasks, but transfer to a new task still requires target information to establish the task specific decision rule. Existing surveys mainly organize time series foundation models by architecture, pretraining objective, training data, or source modality, while the target classification procedure receives less attention. We instead organize foundation models for TSC into three transfer mechanisms: representation transfer, fine-tuning and adaptation, and in-context learning. Alongside the survey, we develop and release the TSC-FM Benchmark, a unified evaluation infrastructure covering 198 TSC datasets and multiple target settings. We use the benchmark to study how downstream classifiers, input settings, and task characteristics affect the assessment of pretrained models. The results show that the same pretrained representation can receive substantially different assessments under different downstream classifiers, that the best reported low shot model differs between univariate and multivariate settings, and that method groups lose accuracy at different rates as the number of classes increases. These findings suggest that transfer capability depends on the match between pretrained knowledge, target task structure, and the target procedure, rather than on the pretrained backbone alone. Future research should both expand the effective range of transfer and reliably identify when a target task falls outside that range.
